There's one thing I still don't understand about the plan.
always: at all times; on every occasion
My grandmother always waters her plants early in the morning.
harmful: causing or likely to cause harm
Excessive sun exposure can be harmful to the skin.
course: used in the phrase 'of course' to mean naturally or certainly
Of course, the final decision still rests with the committee.
tutor: a private teacher who instructs one student or a small group
A good tutor can explain a topic that a teacher with forty students had no time to cover.
topic: a subject that is discussed, written about, or studied
Coming back to a topic after three days means confronting how much has slipped.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
forty: The bus was carrying about forty passengers.
had: past tense of have, used to show possession or a completed action
By the time she arrived, the shop had already closed.
cover: be enough to pay for or deal with something
đáp ứng được, bù đắp cho
Her savings should cover the cost of the repairs.
struggling: trying very hard to deal with a difficult situation
A struggling small business appealed to the bank for more time.
regain: to get something back after losing it
It took months of therapy for him to regain full use of his arm.
confidence: a feeling of being sure about one's own abilities
Winning the first match gave the team real confidence.
scale: the size or extent of something
The scale of the damage surprised even the engineers.
sense: a feeling or awareness of something
A sense of relief washed over her when the results arrived.
have: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses
They have finished the report ahead of schedule.
become: It can take years of practice to become a skilled musician.
compulsory: required by law or a rule; must be done
Wearing a seatbelt is compulsory in almost every country now.
rather: She chose to walk rather than take the crowded bus.
chosen: selected from a number of possibilities
The chosen candidate will start work at the beginning of next month.
governments: groups of people with authority to govern countries
Several governments signed the climate agreement last year.
tried: past tense of try; made an attempt at something
It began to look incomplete when researchers tried the obvious thing and told people the truth.
various: several different types of a thing
The team tried various methods before finding one that worked.
responses: Survey responses showed strong support for the new policy.
limit: the greatest amount or extent allowed
There is a strict limit on how much luggage you can bring.
how: She explained how the machine works in simple terms.
late: near the end of a period of time, or after the expected time
They arrived late because of heavy traffic downtown.
academies: schools or institutions for specialized training or study
Several private academies opened near the capital last decade.
open: not closed; allowing access, movement, or view
They left the window open to let in the cool evening air.
ban: The city plans to ban plastic bags in supermarkets next year.
own: to possess something, or belonging to oneself
Few families in the village own a car of their own.
least: Of all the options, this one costs the least money.
country: a nation with its own government occupying a particular territory
Every country sets its own rules for renewable energy subsidies.
has: has; present tense of have, third person singular
The library has extended its opening hours during exam season.
restrict: The new law will restrict fishing in protected waters.
for-profit: run with the aim of making a financial profit
Several for-profit schools have opened in the growing suburb.
core: the central or most essential part of something
Honesty remains at the core of every successful long-term relationship.
results: things that happen because of actions or events
The test results confirmed what doctors had suspected.
tend: to be likely to do or be something, usually
Older houses in this area tend to have thicker walls.
mixed: combined together to form one substance or group
The paint was mixed carefully to match the original colour.
demand: to require or need something firmly
Modern customers demand fast and reliable delivery service.
stays: continues to be in a place or condition
The lake stays frozen well into early spring.
move: Engineers designed the bridge deck to move slightly in strong wind.
online: connected to or available through the internet
More people now shop online instead of visiting physical stores.
into: moving towards the inside of something
She walked into the room and switched on the light.
homes: The storm damaged dozens of homes along the coast.
vietnam: Vietnam is known for its long coastline and rich cuisine.
offers: presents something for someone to accept, or provides something
The museum offers free entry to students on weekdays.
familiar: The song sounded familiar, though she couldn't remember its name.
example: something that illustrates a general rule or type
The most famous example is the deep blue made from lapis lazuli.
balance: a state in which different things are of equal weight or importance
Finding a balance between work and rest is not always easy.
been: past participle of be, used to show a completed state or experience
They have been friends since primary school.
debated: discussed and argued from different points of view
The proposal was hotly debated at the town meeting.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
newspapers: printed publications containing news, issued regularly
Old newspapers filled the boxes stacked in the attic.
meetings: gatherings of people for discussion or a particular purpose
Her calendar was packed with back-to-back meetings all week.
dinner: the main meal of the day, usually eaten in the evening
We usually have dinner together as a family around seven.
tables: flat pieces of furniture with legs, used for eating or working
Staff arranged extra tables in the hall for the wedding reception.
rules: official instructions stating what may or may not be done
New traffic rules were introduced to reduce accidents.
whether: used to express doubt or choice between alternatives
The useful question is not whether a task is hard, but how it is done.
such: of the type already mentioned or described
Such behaviour will not be tolerated in the workplace.
held: supported or kept in a position; past tense of hold
The bridge was held up by a network of steel cables.
tightened: past tense of tighten; made stricter, firmer, or less loose
The rules on whether teachers may tutor their own students have been tightened more than once.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
each: every one of two or more things, considered separately
Each student received a copy of the new textbook.
welcomed: Each change is welcomed by some parents as protection for their children.
protection: the act of keeping someone or something safe from harm
The vaccine offers strong protection against the most common strains.
criticised: having received expressed disapproval based on perceived faults
The policy was heavily criticised by opposition politicians.
others: other people or things not already mentioned
Some students finished early, while others needed the full hour.
fear: to feel afraid that something bad will happen
Many residents fear that the new road will bring more traffic.
children: plural of child; young human beings
The park was full of children playing after school.
lose: to no longer have something; to be deprived of
If you lose your password, you can reset it online.
source: the place or thing from which something originates
The river's source is a spring high in the mountains.
help: She asked her neighbour for help moving the sofa.
rely: to depend on someone or something with confidence
Many farmers rely on rainfall rather than irrigation systems.
suggests: puts forward an idea; indicates a possibility
The evidence suggests that the drug works better in younger patients.
symptom: a sign that shows a person has an illness or a problem exists
A persistent cough can be an early symptom of the illness.
disease: an illness affecting a person, animal, or plant
Doctors are working to find a cure for the rare disease.
carries: transports or supports something while moving
The delivery van carries fresh vegetables to markets every morning.
weight: how heavy something is; a heavy object
That turn moves the wheels back underneath the falling weight of the rider.
keep: to continue having or doing something; to maintain
Please keep this document safe until the meeting next week.
buying: Buying in bulk usually works out cheaper per item.
reducing: making something smaller or less in amount
The factory invested in machinery aimed at reducing water waste.
pressure: a feeling of stress caused by demands or difficulties
The manager felt under pressure to finish the project by Friday.
probably: almost certainly; likely to be true
He is probably still at work; his car is not in the driveway.
means: A nod usually means agreement in most cultures.
changing: The climate is changing faster in polar regions than elsewhere.
selected: Only a handful of candidates were selected for the final interview.
closing: shutting, or coming to an end
Closing the shop early gave staff time to rest before the holiday.
classrooms: plural of classroom; rooms where students are taught
The school built five new classrooms to handle growing enrolment.
shops: places where goods are sold to the public
Small shops line the narrow streets of the old town.
systems: sets of things working together as connected wholes
Several legal systems now recognise rivers as having rights.
already: before now or before a particular time
By the time we arrived, the meeting had already started.
combine: to join two or more things together to form a single thing
The recipe asks you to combine flour, sugar and butter first.
final: This is the final chapter of the novel.
marks: shows or indicates something, or makes a visible sign on it
A small star marks the correct answer on the page.
several: more than two but not very many
Several guests arrived late because of the traffic.
schoolwork: work done by students as part of their studies
He struggled to finish his schoolwork before the deadline.
everything: all things; the whole of something
Warmth speeds everything up, and dough rises quickly in a hot kitchen.
slow: The traffic was slow because of the heavy rain.
politically: in a way that relates to politics or government
The region remained politically unstable for nearly a decade.
difficult: not easy to do or understand
Learning a new language can be difficult at first.
until: up to the point in time that something happens
It worked until it did not.
then: at that time, or next in a sequence of events
We finished dinner, and then we watched a film together.
studying: the act of spending time learning about a subject
Studying for a few hours each evening improved her grades.
bell: a hollow metal device that rings when struck
The old church bell rang loudly across the quiet village square.
